title: Why use QR Control: for retailers, brands and advertisers
summary: QR Control turns a store screen into a personalised, interactive experience that runs across the screen and the customer's phone. This explains the value for retailers, brands and advertisers.
seoTitle: Why Use QR Control: Benefits for Retailers, Brands and Advertisers
metaDescription: See how QR Control turns store screens into personalised, interactive experiences, and what retailers, brands and advertisers gain from it.
directAnswer: QR Control lets a customer connect their phone to a store screen and get a personalised, interactive experience across both. Retailers drive engagement and capture intent for staff. Brands get a guided zone. Advertisers open a relationship they can continue through remarketing.
questionVariants: Why should we use QR Control?
What are the benefits of QR Control for retailers?
How can brands use QR Control in store?
How does QR Control help advertisers?
What is the value of QR Control?
Why let customers connect their phone to a store screen?
bodyMd:
QR Control lets a customer take over a store screen from their own phone, and it is worth using because the experience that follows is built around them. When a customer checks in to a store, Personalisation Hub knows who they are. When they connect their phone to a screen, the platform opens a hyper-personalised experience that runs in step across the screen and their mobile store site or app. It draws on everything it knows about that customer. Instead of watching a screen, they chat, play, learn and explore.

This page explains the value for each audience. For the mechanics, see How QR Control works.

What changes for the customer

A passive screen shows everyone the same thing. With QR Control, the customer scans a code and their phone connects to the screen. From then on the screen and the phone work together, and both reflect who the customer is, what they have done before and what they are looking for right now.

  • Interactive chat. The customer asks questions and gets answers shaped by their profile.
  • Games and challenges. Short, playful experiences hold attention far longer than a loop of video.
  • Educational and brand content. Guides, demonstrations and stories are chosen for that customer, and they choose what to explore next.

Because the phone is the controller, the customer decides what happens on the screen. That is what turns viewing into interaction.

Why retailers use QR Control

  • Draw customers to the right part of the store. Place QR Control screens in specific sections, such as a demonstration area or a service counter, and give customers a reason to walk up and interact with them.
  • Capture real intent. What a customer chooses to explore on the screen shows what they actually want, such as a particular model, colour or service. It is a stronger signal than browsing alone.
  • Hand over to staff faster. That intent passes to the member of staff who picks the customer up. The conversation starts from what the customer already wants, so it is shorter and more useful for both sides.
  • Earn from screens and brand zones. Interactive screens are more valuable to brands than passive ones, so retailers can monetise screens and dedicated brand zones with engagement that brands can see.

Why brands use QR Control

A brand can have its own section or zone in a store. A beauty brand's zone in a pharmacy is a typical example. One screen in that zone can run several experiences, and QR Control guides each customer to the one that fits them.

  • A guided route. The customer is steered toward what interests them, such as skincare advice, a shade finder or a how-to video, and not left to work out where to start.
  • Several experiences on one screen. A single display can serve many customers one after another, each with a different experience.
  • Richer content than a loop allows. The brand can offer tutorials, product stories and games that the customer chooses, so the time they spend in the zone is real engagement.

Why advertisers use QR Control

For an advertiser, an interaction is the start of a relationship with the customer. A customer who has chosen to engage with an advertiser's content on the screen has shown real interest.

  • An engagement to build on. The interaction gives the advertiser a customer to follow up with, where a passive view gives only an impression.
  • Remarketing beyond the store. The relationship can continue through remarketing at other touch points, reached through demand-side platforms (DSPs), so the conversation carries on after the customer leaves.

Where to start

Pick the screens and zones where a customer's attention matters most, and enable QR Control there. See Enable QR Control on a display and Enable QR Control and set the default QR code settings.
